brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;half-n is present, counts piece=1, total parts=2. No other base has been added. A half base is the only variant that offers a drawer socket; a full base offers zero drawer sockets.

requirements.requirement: Nothing else added beside or on top of it (no adjacent or stacked cells)
requirements.evidence: get_build shows only q=0,r=0,level=0 occupied. find_sockets piece shows 6 adjacent cells empty, level 1 empty. No covers/caps added to respect literal brief and house-rule exception for smallest build — left uncapped and unlocked as requested.

requirements.requirement: Five drawers in the single base
requirements.evidence: Maximum 1 drawer per half-base cut face enforced by configurator. drawer:0#0,0#cut fitted via s104 (key s). Second addDrawer at same at/key refused ALREADY_FITTED ('this cut face already carries a drawer'). Notch/bay drawers require two/three touching bases beside an empty cell (not available without violating 'nothing beside'), so cannot reach 5 in one cell. Build shows 1 drawer, 4 short.

finish.summary: Built the maximum allowed under the 'single base, nothing beside/on top' constraint: one half-n hex base with its single cut-face drawer. Verified by configurator that a second drawer on the same base is refused ALREADY_FITTED, and that notch/bay drawer types need extra bases beside the target cell, which would violate the brief. Five drawers in one unstacked, isolated cell is not possible in Hex Cluster; stacking five half-levels could provide five drawers but was not built because it directly violates 'nothing on top'.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: One base, five drawers — I'll map your base to see how to fit all five.
